products.name: Anna's Hummingbird — Matted 8×10 Print
products.short: An adult male Anna's Hummingbird at rest on salvia — the hummingbird that stays through a California winter.
products.description:
Anna's Hummingbirds don't leave. While other hummingbirds follow the bloom south, these stay through a California winter — small, fierce, and permanent. This adult male is painted at rest rather than in flight, which is how you almost never see them: perched on a salvia stem, gorget lit magenta, close enough to count the scaled green feathers across his back.

Best hung close, where the feather detail reads.
specs: Giclée print of an original watercolor

Signed and titled in pencil

Printed locally in San Diego

products.name: Burrowing Owl — Matted 8×10 Print
products.short: A Burrowing Owl mid head-tilt beside desert dandelion — a ground-dwelling owl in decline across California.
products.description:
Burrowing Owls live underground. They nest in old ground squirrel burrows in open grassland, stand about nine inches tall, and hunt at dawn and dusk on long bare legs. This one is caught mid head-tilt — the gesture everyone who has met one remembers — beside a stand of desert dandelion.

They are disappearing across California as the open ground they depend on gets developed. Painting one felt like the least I could do, and the most: a chance to make someone look closely at a bird they may never have known was living down the road.

Warm browns and yellow against a pale ground. It reads well in an entryway or above a desk.
specs: Giclée print of an original watercolor
8×10 image, matted to 11×14 with a white bevel-cut mat
Signed and titled in pencil

Printed locally in San Diego

products.name: Emergence — Matted 8×10 Print
products.short: A monarch on showy milkweed — the one plant its caterpillars can eat, painted as a single system.
products.description:
Monarch caterpillars can eat exactly one thing: milkweed. No milkweed, no monarchs — the two are locked together, and the collapse of one is the collapse of the other. This painting puts them in the same frame where they belong: a monarch resting against the broad leaves of showy milkweed under a deep blue wash.

Titled Emergence, for what milkweed makes possible.

Deep blue against orange — it carries color into a room.
specs: Giclée print of an original watercolor
8×10 image, matted to 11×14 with a white bevel-cut mat

products.name: Frieda's African Violets — Matted 8×10 Print
products.short: An oil painting of African violets, named for my great-grandmother Frieda — a midwife, an entrepreneur, and a grower of flowers.
products.description:
I named this painting after a woman I never met. Frieda was my great-grandmother, and I grew up on stories of her — a midwife, an entrepreneur, a grower of flowers. She went after the life she wanted and built it against the odds. She grew African violets on her windowsills.

My mother always kept African violets. Now I do too. And when I came back to painting after a long time away, this is the flower I came back to — the one that started it all.

Painted in oil against a dark ground, the light catches what most people never notice about them: the leaves are furred, silver at every edge, and the petals hold a dozen shades between white and deep purple. The original was accepted into the San Diego County Fair fine art exhibit and stays with my family. This print is how it travels.

Dark ground, soft light. It settles a space rather than brightening it.
specs: Giclée print of an original oil painting
8×10 image, matted to 11×14 with a white bevel-cut mat
Signed and titled in pencil
Fits any standard 11×14 frame — frame not included
Printed locally in San Diego

products.short: A Western Tanager among manzanita — flame-orange and yellow, here only on migration.
products.description:
The first time you see a Western Tanager, you assume something has escaped. A flame-orange head, a body of hard yellow, black wings — it looks like it belongs somewhere tropical, and then it's gone. They pass through California on migration, which means seeing one is a matter of being outside at the right week of the right month.

Painted perched among manzanita, with its berries hanging heavy on the branch.

Strong color against a pale ground. It holds up on a dim wall.

products.short: A federally threatened California Gnatcatcher on California buckwheat — the small gray bird most people walk past.
products.description:
A small gray bird that most people walk past. The coastal California Gnatcatcher is federally threatened, and its whole existence depends on the low coastal scrub that gets cleared first and defended last. Protect that habitat and you keep the gnatcatcher. It's that direct.

Painted at close range on California buckwheat, so you can see what's actually there: soft gray, a black cap, a long dark tail held at an angle, and the pale clustered blooms it moves through.

Muted grays, dusty greens, soft pink. Quiet on a wall.
